neet_phy_u13_t01_2.working: Inside the wire, B = μ0Ir/(2πR²). At r = 1 cm, R = 2 cm this is μ0I/(2π)×25. Outside, B = μ0I/(2πr); at r = 4 cm this is μ0I/(2π)×25. So B1/B2 = 1.

neet_phy_u13_t01_3.working: n = 500/0.5 = 1000 per m. Field at the centre = μ0nI = 2.51×10^-3 T. At the end the field is half of this, 1.26×10^-3 T.

neet_phy_u13_t01_4.working: Outside a straight wire B ∝ 1/r (A-III). Inside a solid wire B ∝ r (B-II). Inside a hollow pipe no current is enclosed, so B = 0 (C-I). Inside a solenoid B = μ0nI (D-IV).

neet_phy_u13_t01_5.working: A is true: the line integral depends only on enclosed current. B is true. C is true. D is false: doubling length halves n, so the field halves. E is false: the field is zero on the axis. Correct set is A, B, C.
